# Open questions — jpegxl-rs

What is not yet known, and what has since been answered.

## Open

### Promote the case-table crossing predictor (feature case-predictor, now v2 with structure features and 347 cases) to the default controller?

`open` · `@jpegxl-rs.question.promote-case-predictor-2026-09-02/2` · **at risk**

Feature `case-predictor` replaces the qpv2-st-1 linear knot model's first guess with the distance-weighted mean of the nearest labelled images' oracle crossing curves. Version 2 (2026-09-02 evening, @jpegxl-rs.observation.case-predictor-v2-paintings-study-2026-09-02): the still265 structure pass is ported (preanalysis.rs) and attached at frame preparation, the table is 347 cases over the old corpus plus 258 paintings, the neighbour geometry (per-feature weights, k 2 with a 3x adaptive cut, a quarter-spread offset, spread threshold 0.405) was searched against the simulated Balanced + Fast probe count under leave-one-family-out on calibration+development families only, and any table fallback now hands the frame to the knot model, i.e. behaves exactly as the default controller. Preregistered blind trial on 52 never-seen paintings: Balanced 0 floor violations on 364 cells, byte geomean 0.990, worst cell 1.092, probes 2.21 -> 1.77, cells at <= 2 probes 242 -> 322 (@jpegxl-rs.evidence.case-predictor-v2-blind-paintings-balanced-2026-09-02); Fast 0 floor / 0 errors on 208 cells, 0.977, 1.84 -> 1.73 (@jpegxl-rs.evidence.case-predictor-v2-blind-paintings-fast-2026-09-02); old-corpus holdout (in the table) 0 floor, 0.981, 3.13 -> 1.64 (@jpegxl-rs.evidence.case-predictor-v2-corpus-holdout-in-table-2026-09-02); thread identity 9/9; gates green. Verdict: Pass on every preregistered criterion in round 2; round 1 (legacy-start fallback) was Partial on one 1.41x fallback cell, and the fallback change was made after seeing it (disclosed). Against promotion: the landed v1 table without paintings made paintings WORSE (2.21 -> 2.49 probes, @jpegxl-rs.evidence.case-predictor-v1-table-on-paintings-2026-09-02), so the predictor is only as good as the table's coverage of the content a user encodes — camera photographs (12-50 MP) still have no close case; sub-kilobyte synthetic gradients keep a tail (one 416 -> 1074 byte cell); it changes every quality stream. Should v2 join `default`? If yes, the promotion commit adds the feature to the policy crate's default set and notes that pre-promotion byte baselines are superseded; the next accuracy lever is labelled camera photographs and screenshots (coverage), not model structure.

> **At risk** at depth 1 via `supported_by` → `@jpegxl-rs.observation.case-table-first-guess-study-2026-09-02/1` (stale: `watches "JPXL/tools/quality_predictor_v2.py"` was matched by `2b1a0555`, which touched `JPXL/tools/quality_predictor_v2.py`.). See [REVIEW-REQUIRED.md](REVIEW-REQUIRED.md#promote-the-case-table-crossing-predictor-feature-case-predictor-now-v2-with-structure-features-and-347-cases-to-the-default-controller).

### Route text/line-art content using the bpg-rs still265 preanalysis classifier?

`open` · `@jpegxl-rs.question.route-text-lineart-via-bpg-preanalysis/1`

JPXL's weakest content class against cjxl is synthetic text/line-art (up to +135% bytes at matched score, @jpegxl-rs.evidence.pqc-pr4-byte-neutral-2026-08-22). The operator points at existing first-party detection code: bpg-rs crates/still265/src/preanalysis.rs classifies 32x32 cells into 7 RegionClass values including TextLike (dense axis-aligned low-entropy edges, a text/line-art proxy) from cheap per-cell features (edge density, orientation entropy, direction dominance, flat ratio, chroma activity) plus a contextual saliency pass, with frame-level class_counts(). Should JPXL port or consume this preanalysis to detect screenshot/line-art frames and route them differently (modular/palette path, different effort or quantization policy)? Same-author code, so no licensing question; the open questions are the porting seam (jpxl-analysis vs a shared crate) and what the router changes (mode choice is a policy change under Contract B).

### Price only the coarsest feasible finalist? (1.3% rare-byte-change tail)

`open` · `@jpegxl-rs.question.single-finalist-pricing-contract-b/1` · **at risk**

Should the Balanced quality search price only its coarsest feasible finalist instead of up to two (quality.rs solve_baseline: budget.exact_prices.clamp(1,2), keeping the smallest stream)? The shadow corpus shows the second exact price buys nothing on 75/76 two-finalist cells (the coarsest feasible finalist is also the smaller stream, median 9.3% smaller) but would have won on 1 cell (1.3%, a 700x700 synthetic at adjacent rungs where entropy training flipped the ordering by 18 bytes), so skipping it saves roughly one entropy training plus one emission per multi-finalist encode - about 100 ms on the 12 MP anchor - at the cost of a rare larger stream. This can alter emitted bytes, so it is a Contract B decision: promotion gates are the standing matched-rate and quality A/B screens and the operator's explicit acceptance of the 1.3% rare-byte-change tail.

> **At risk** at depth 1 via `supported_by` → `@jpegxl-rs.observation.probe-contract-b-shadow-2026-09-01/1` (stale: `watches "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode-policy/src/quality_prediction.rs"` was matched by `2b1a0555`, which touched `JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode-policy/src/quality_prediction.rs`.). See [REVIEW-REQUIRED.md](REVIEW-REQUIRED.md#price-only-the-coarsest-feasible-finalist-13-rare-byte-change-tail).

## Recently closed

### Low-target one pass: below which target, and does one pass mean one verified probe or no verification?

`resolved` · `@jpegxl-rs.question.low-target-one-pass-parameters/2`

Low-target one pass: below which target, and does one pass mean one verified probe or no verification?

**Resolution.** Neither parameter was needed. The operator delegated the decision ('do what you think is best for speed vs quality/size efficiency; if dropping probes for low quality encodes is not optimal and overly complex then do something else'). The low targets were slow not for want of a one-pass rule but because the crossing aim (threshold + reserve × loss) lay outside the fixed one-point accept band below Balanced 66.7 / Fast 83.3, so a landing on the aim never stopped the search (@jpegxl-rs.observation.crossing-aim-outside-accept-band-below-67-2026-09-02). The reserve-coupled band fixes that at every target with the floor kept and every probe still verified (@jpegxl-rs.decision.promote-reserve-coupled-band-2026-09-02). A literal unverified or first-probe-only pass was rejected: on photos at target 30 the predictor's first landing is 0.3-0.5 ln effective scale above the crossing, a large byte cost, not a saving (@jpegxl-rs.observation.qpv2-photo-low-target-bias-2026-09-02); the remaining low-target probes are the predictor's.

**Resolved by** [Promote the reserve-coupled accept band to the default Balanced/Fast controller (delegated decision)](DECISION-HISTORY.md#revision-1--promote-the-reserve-coupled-accept-band-to-the-default-balancedfast-controller-delegated-decision) `@jpegxl-rs.decision.promote-reserve-coupled-band-2026-09-02/1`

### Recalibrate qpv2 to raise the 4.3% one-shot stop rate?

`resolved` · `@jpegxl-rs.question.one-shot-calibration-contract-b/4`

Should the qpv2 prediction be recalibrated to raise the one-shot stop rate (currently 4/94 = 4.3% on the quality corpus at score 85 balanced)? The stop mechanism is already proven safe where it fires (N3, 2026-08-29: every stopped cell chose exactly the rung the full search would), and the shadow corpus attributes every missed stop to calibration: 9 of 13 confident cells overshot by more than the 1.0-point band (the candidate rung is a conservative upper quantile; predicted-rung/winner-rung median 1.34) and 8 of 12 in-band cells were blocked by the confidence gate. Each converted cell saves two of about 3.5 baseline pixel probes - roughly 850-900 ms on the 12 MP anchor. This can alter which rung wins and the emitted bytes, so it is a Contract B decision: promotion gates are a corpus-wide byte-delta and quality A/B screen and the operator's acceptance of the changed rung distribution; a first zero-risk step is retraining the model on the existing corpus traces and shadow-measuring the would-have-stopped rate without touching the encoder.

**Resolution.** Resolved 2026-09-02 by the operator's promotion decision (@jpegxl-rs.decision.promote-corrected-stop-and-median-start-2026-09-02): not by recalibrating the model, which cannot be promoted (@jpegxl-rs.evidence.qpv2-current-corpus-retrain-2026-09-02), but by dropping the confidence gate on the one-shot stop (`trusted-first-probe`, byte-identical where it fires) and adding the gated corrected stop and the large-frame median start, which together take the corpus from 3.462 to 3.022 pixel probes per encode with zero floor violations and byte geomean 0.995 (@jpegxl-rs.observation.contract-b-corrected-stop-trial-2026-09-02). The one-shot stop rate at q85 is now 12/91; the remaining probes are bound by first-probe predictor accuracy (@jpegxl-rs.assessment.two-probe-path-is-predictor-bound-2026-09-02) and, at low targets, by the open low-target one-pass rule (@jpegxl-rs.question.low-target-one-pass-parameters).

**Resolved by** [Promote the corrected stop (with the trusted first probe) and the large-frame median start to the default Balanced/Fast controller](DECISION-HISTORY.md#revision-1--promote-the-corrected-stop-with-the-trusted-first-probe-and-the-large-frame-median-start-to-the-default-balancedfast-controller) `@jpegxl-rs.decision.promote-corrected-stop-and-median-start-2026-09-02/1`

### Where does the frequency weight's shape come from, now that a detection CSF is ruled out?

`resolved` · `@jpegxl-rs.question.which-perceptual-weight-crosses-the-cleanroom-line/2`

Phase 6.3 established that frequency weighting drives the cover objective (butteraugli moves -16.4% to +32.4%, SSIMULACRA2 up to +4.37, against transform size's near-null) and that a Mannos-Sakrison detection CSF is the wrong curve, failing its pre-registered agreement check at 3.14x worst-bin ratio and r = 0.408. Measurement and screen agree on what the right curve looks like: far flatter at high frequency than a detection CSF, with no low-frequency dip.

The obvious next step -- give the weight the measured shape -- crosses the line the workspace manifest draws around the butteraugli dependency: a table fitted to that metric's response makes this project's perceptual model a derivative of libjxl's rather than its own, with licence and provenance consequences. AGENTS.md section 2 makes that a decision to record before it is taken, not an implementation detail.

Three options, in the preference order Phase 6.3 recorded:

1. A distortion-visibility model from open literature rather than a detection CSF. Same clean-room standing as Phase 6.3, and the screen has now characterised what it must look like, so the search is well-posed rather than open-ended. Keeps the perceptual model this project's own.

2. A two-parameter analytic shape -- low-frequency plateau plus a gentle rolloff -- whose parameters are set from the encoder's own quantization geometry (the I.2.5 default matrices, whose per-size step ratios Phase 6.2 already measured) rather than from butteraugli, then checked against the Phase 6.2 measurement the same way Phase 6.3 checked Mannos-Sakrison.

3. Fit the measured curve, explicitly recorded as a decision that the perceptual model becomes libjxl-derived.

A fourth possibility the rate split raises: the 1 bpp arm is already a uniform SSIMULACRA2 win and a 5-of-7 butteraugli win, and the 2 bpp arm is where it fails. That is evidence the correct weight interacts with which coefficients survive quantization -- something no static table can capture, and a pointer at HfQuantizer::choose, which is still nearest-reconstruction rather than RD-optimal. The next round may belong on the quantizer rather than on a better table.

**Blocks**
- `completed` [Phase 6.4: measure chroma frequency response at a controlled operating point](ACTIVE-WORK.md#phase-64-measure-chroma-frequency-response-at-a-controlled-operating-point) `@jpegxl-rs.work.arch-phase6-4-chroma-controlled-operating-point/1`

**Resolution.** Resolved by Phase 6.5 without crossing the line. Option 1 is closed. The canonical DCT-domain per-coefficient models -- Ahumada & Peterson (1992), Peterson, Ahumada & Watson (1993), Watson's DCTune (1993), Nill (1985) -- are all detection-threshold models: band-pass with a low-frequency dip and a high-frequency rolloff HARDER than Mannos-Sakrison. AP92 predicts about 0.037 of peak sensitivity at Nyquist where measurement says about 1.05, roughly 28x off against Mannos-Sakrison's 3.1x, so adopting any of them would be strictly worse than what Phase 6.3 rejected. Georgeson & Sullivan (1975) explain why: above threshold, perceived contrast becomes largely independent of spatial frequency (contrast constancy), so a detection CSF -- which describes seeing a grating on a blank field -- is the wrong regime for judging quantization error in real content, where low-frequency error is highly visible. Option 2 supplies the answer, in corrected form. The shape comes from the standard's own I.2.5 DCT8x8 matrix, read as a curve in normalised radial frequency and resampled onto every transform's grid -- NOT from each size's own matrix, which is the 1/step^2 weighting Phase 6.2 falsified, because the matrices are per-size tuned and disagree 3.34x across sizes. It scores median 1.41x against the measured target, against the CSF's 2.06x and the 1.18x ceiling of a curve fitted directly to butteraugli. Option 3 is declined. The remaining 1.41x-to-1.18x margin does not justify making the perceptual model libjxl-derived. The model stays this project's own, sourced from the standard. The fourth possibility this record raised -- that the right weight interacts with which coefficients survive quantization -- is now supported rather than speculative: Phase 6.5's donor is a large win at 0.5 bpp, clear at 1 bpp, neutral at 2 and a no-op at 4 bpp. Carried forward in jpegxl-rs.observation.donor-weight-wins-at-low-rate-and-fades-2026-08-12, whose conclusion is that the next round belongs on HfQuantizer::choose, still nearest-reconstruction rather than RD-optimal.

**Resolved by** [The standard's own DCT8x8 matrix donates the best frequency weight yet: a large low-rate win fading to a no-op by 4 bpp, which points at the quantizer](CURRENT-STATE.md#the-standards-own-dct8x8-matrix-donates-the-best-frequency-weight-yet-a-large-low-rate-win-fading-to-a-no-op-by-4-bpp-which-points-at-the-quantizer) `@jpegxl-rs.observation.donor-weight-wins-at-low-rate-and-fades-2026-08-12/2`
